events.title: The September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks kill thousands of people in the United States. Communities mourn and help those affected.

events.title: Apple introduces the iPod
events.description: A pocket-sized digital music player becomes a new product for the computer maker.

events.title: Euro cash enters everyday use
events.description: Twelve countries introduce euro notes and coins.

events.title: Columbia is lost
events.description: The space shuttle breaks apart during its return to Earth, killing its seven crew members.

what_happened_next.text:
Occidental Petroleum more than tripled, leading these choices. Apple gained, but Amazon lost about one-third. The US share basket also finished lower, while bonds gained. The opening month’s excitement about the internet did not describe every business, and it did not make all online investments successful.

Apple introduced the iPod in October 2001, expanding beyond computers into portable music. The business itself was changing while investors held its shares.

During the five years, the September 11 attacks brought devastating human losses. Euro notes and coins entered everyday use in 2002. The Columbia shuttle was lost in 2003, killing its seven crew members. The future contained important events that nobody could read from the opening page.

The two internet-related shares are a useful comparison. Apple finished higher while Amazon finished lower, so one label did not describe both results. Bonds followed a different route again. If you spread money across choices, your final result would combine those gains and losses. The most talked-about industry was not the only place an investor could put money, and the strongest company story was not a guaranteed price forecast.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Online shopping, technology wealth and executive rewards filled the news. An oil-drilling dispute showed that older industries still mattered too.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The seven investments followed different paths. Bonds gained while the broad US basket fell, and even the two technology-related companies had different results.
reflection.what_faded_away: A famous leader’s reward and an online-shopping stunt did not predict five-year returns. Public attention was not the same as investment value.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Nobody knew the final ranking or the crises ahead. It would have been easy to overlook a less fashionable industry while reading exciting technology stories.
